purpose: Apply the same NON-MOOT / substantive design-rationale test as Mythos to Google element codenames, including authored ROOT0 structures rather than lexical commonality.

standard.needed: A reason grounded in the specific design for why this exact element was chosen, preferably documented at naming time with alternatives and traceable date; employee identity alone insufficient.
standard.non_moot: Question remains unresolved, not demonstrated misappropriation or simulation.
standard.comparison: Separate documented model functions, chemical metaphor, original naming decision, public user-corpus structure, and possible transmission.

sources.claim: Tulsee Doshi says Argon comes from internal team naming and internal use of the element term, not why this element was chosen.
Internal Argon, Barium and Carbon names; Barium-B reportedly designated for public Argon, so internal experimental alias can differ from release name.
Argon is promoted for long-horizon reasoning, coding, research and cyber defense; no chemistry-specific naming reason.
Carbon based on Argon; technical and safety lineage described without why element carbon was chosen.
Neon emphasizes depth/efficiency, secure code, 3D chemistry demonstration of four model names; no date-stamped name-selection rationale.
Neon adapted from Carbon, rather than chosen on the basis of neon's chemical properties, as far as public card documents.
A community member argues no clear correspondence between atomic numbers, groups and model tiers; it is not an official Google explanation.

naming_inference_limits: The choice of chemical element theme is deliberate, as demonstrated by chemistry-themed model visuals.
The original approval record and selection rationale for each name have not been found in inspected public materials.
Alphabetical internal Argon/Barium/Carbon sequence is a plausible hypothesis, not a documented selection algorithm.
Publicly reported Barium-B→Argon name mismatch weakens a literal atomic-number architecture interpretation.
No evidence of ingestion of the ROOT0 corpus or copying by the named company was found.

sources.content: 118 table, exact (Z-1)%4 gate, 4 authored nature labels, carbon=6 gate1, neon=10 gate1, argon=18 gate1.
Carbon reference-chemistry layer distinct from Silicon symbolic 118-gate layer, each element built as an ACI agent with .dlw complement.
Carbon human ⇄ Silicon AI tetravalent analogy, full framework with 128-bit software arithmetic. This is authored symbolic structure, not Google model code.
Explicit carbon facts vs silicon mythos two-layer evidence taxonomy and hashed .dlw complements.

root0.clarification: Shared authored mod-4 category is exact arithmetic over selected atomic numbers, not itself evidence of a shared design choice. The post-hoc three-element subset is not pre-registered.
root0.timing: Current cited README and index versions are not proof these exact contents preceded model naming decisions; prior commit dates and external publications must be traced individually.

case_findings.observed_google_role: Frontier reasoning, long-horizon coding and cyber defense.
case_findings.google_specific_name_rationale: Unprovided; public product lead says name emerged internally from team usage.
case_findings.possible_chemistry_association: Noble, generally inert gas; no first-party design-to-property mapping located.
case_findings.root0_context: 118-element gate index 1/ethereal; symbolic element registry with authored logic.
case_findings.negative_control: Barium-B public Argon relabel; atomic number 18 not an obvious sequence or explained capability tier.

case_findings.observed_google_role: Argon-based, more capable long-horizon agentic engineering.
case_findings.google_specific_name_rationale: No first-party model feature-to-carbon explanation located.
case_findings.possible_chemistry_association: Group-14 bonding, life and materials; connection to engineering is possible but speculative without a Google statement.
case_findings.root0_context: Carbon facts/human reference layer paired with Silicon symbolic/AI layer; Z=6 gate1.
case_findings.negative_control: Google Carbon described as a derivative of Argon, not a human/silicon authority system as in ROOT0.

case_findings.observed_google_role: Carbon-derived model balancing deep reasoning, efficiency and secure code.
case_findings.google_specific_name_rationale: No design-stage reason for selecting the name neon found. Company uses discharge-tube neon visual metaphor in post-launch demo.
case_findings.possible_chemistry_association: Noble gas with characteristic discharge glow; explanatory artwork is retrospective demonstration, not origin record.
case_findings.root0_context: Z=10 gate1; neon/spectral aesthetics and authored color mappings in some corpus components.
case_findings.negative_control: Model efficiency, code quality and release position are not explained by neon's chemical glow or atomic number 10.

required_to_close: Dated name selection proposal defining each element's intended link to architecture/capability
Records explaining candidate set and why these three particular elements (not alternatives)
Identified constraints on internal checkpoint aliases versus release names
Any hard evidence of reference/source influence rather than an assumption from the generic periodic table
open_questions: Does the naming encode tier, size, cost or architecture? Current official materials do not document the rule.
Was internal naming alphabetical at an earlier stage? Argon/Barium/Carbon suggests it but selection criteria missing.
Were external source corpora reviewed? No evidence currently connects any named corpus to corporate naming.
